info.title: Graffiti Merge: Street Empire game build

messages.text:
"BUILD A COMPLETE 2D PIXEL ART GAME: GRAFFITI MERGE

Create a complete, playable 2D pixel-art merge and idle tycoon game called Graffiti Merge: Street Empire.

This is a full game development request. Build the actual working game, not a prototype, mockup, or static interface.

IMPORTANT: Keep the project technically simple, stable, and lightweight. Prioritize a finished, functional game over a large number of complicated features.

1. GAME STYLE AND VISUAL DESIGN

- 2D pixel-art graphics.
- Colorful, detailed, hand-crafted pixel-art aesthetic.
- Urban graffiti and street-art atmosphere.
- Brick walls, paint cans, markers, pencils, paint buckets, spray caps and graffiti equipment.
- Attractive character sprites with simple animations.
- Smooth and satisfying merge animations.
- Small visual effects when artists finish drawings and collect rewards.
- Clear, readable interface.

Avoid futuristic designs, neon sci-fi interfaces, excessive glowing effects, and generic mobile game templates.

The game should look like a charming pixel-art street graffiti workshop.

2. MAIN GAMEPLAY LOOP

The player owns a small graffiti workshop.

The main gameplay consists of three connected activities:

A. MERGE EQUIPMENT

- A dedicated merge board contains graffiti equipment.
- New basic items periodically appear in empty board cells.
- The player can drag and drop items.
- Combining two identical items of the same level creates one item of the next level.
- Higher-level equipment is more valuable and produces more income.
- Make merging satisfying with visual feedback and sound effects.

Example equipment progression:

Level 1: Pencil.
Level 2: Sketch marker.
Level 3: Paint marker.
Level 4: Spray paint can.
Level 5: Professional spray can.
Level 6: Premium graffiti equipment.

Create simple pixel-art icons for every equipment level.

B. ARTISTS AND GRAFFITI

- The workshop has one starting graffiti artist.
- Artists automatically take available equipment and start drawing on the graffiti wall.
- Show an actual drawing animation when an artist works.
- When a drawing is completed, the player receives coins.
- Better equipment increases the value of completed artwork.
- Higher-level artists work faster and earn more coins.
- Multiple artists can work simultaneously.

The player must clearly see the artists doing their jobs. Do not replace this mechanic with invisible background calculations.

C. ECONOMY AND UPGRADES

Coins are the main currency.

Allow players to spend coins on:

1. Hiring additional graffiti artists.
2. Increasing artist efficiency.
3. Improving equipment.
4. Increasing the speed of new equipment generation.
5. Expanding the merge board.
6. Upgrading the graffiti wall.
7. Unlocking new workshop locations.

Every upgrade must have a visible effect on gameplay.

3. PROGRESSION

Create a simple but satisfying progression system.

Start with:

- One artist.
- A small brick wall.
- Basic graffiti equipment.
- A small merge board.
- Low starting income.

As the player progresses:

- More artists become available.
- Better equipment becomes unlockable.
- Artists work faster.
- Graffiti becomes more valuable.
- New walls and workshop environments become available.

Use gradually increasing upgrade prices.

Progression should feel rewarding but NOT too fast.

The player should have meaningful goals and should not unlock everything within a few minutes.

4. EXTRA GAMEPLAY FEATURES

Add these features only if they can be implemented reliably:

- Achievement system with rewards.
- Collection book showing discovered equipment.
- Combo bonus for several successful merges.
- Milestone rewards for reaching certain income levels.
- Different graffiti wall designs.
- Small unlockable visual decorations for the workshop.

Keep these systems simple. Do not build complicated quest chains or unnecessary progression trees.

5. USER INTERFACE

Create a clean, attractive pixel-art interface.

Display:

- Current coin balance.
- Merge board.
- Active graffiti artists.
- Current workshop level.
- Upgrade buttons and their prices.
- Progress toward the next unlock.

Make all buttons functional.

The interface must be readable on Android mobile screens.

Use large touch-friendly buttons and make drag-and-drop merging comfortable on a touchscreen.

6. GAME BALANCE

Balance is extremely important.

- Do not make money accumulate ridiculously fast.
- Do not make equipment spawn too frequently.
- Do not make upgrades almost free.
- Do not make artists finish drawings instantly.
- Avoid excessive notifications and popups.
- Keep animations short and smooth.
- Give every upgrade a meaningful but balanced benefit.

The game should be relaxing, addictive, and rewarding without overwhelming the player.

7. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

IMPORTANT: Do not overcomplicate the project.

- Use simple, reliable game systems.
- Use a single main gameplay scene whenever possible.
- Avoid unnecessary external libraries and dependencies.
- Do not implement online multiplayer.
- Do not require a server or external accounts.
- Save coins, equipment, artists, upgrades and progression locally.
- Make the game playable offline.
- Support the Russian language throughout the entire interface.
- Add a language setting with Russian as the default language.
- Make the layout responsive for mobile screens.

Do not create complicated physics, weather systems, complex AI, procedural worlds, or unnecessary simulation mechanics.

8. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Follow this exact priority order:

PRIORITY 1:
Build the playable core game:

- Working merge board.
- Item generation.
- Drag-and-drop merging.
- Artists that collect equipment and draw graffiti.
- Working coin rewards.
- Functional upgrades.

PRIORITY 2:
Add progression:

- Additional artists.
- Equipment levels.
- Workshop upgrades.
- Increasing income and costs.

PRIORITY 3:
Add achievements, collections, visual decorations and additional locations.

If a feature threatens stability or completion, simplify that feature instead of breaking the main game.

9. FINAL TESTING

Before declaring the game finished, test the actual gameplay.

Verify that:

- New items spawn correctly.
- Items can be dragged.
- Identical items merge correctly.
- Different items cannot merge.
- Artists correctly start and finish drawing.
- Coins are awarded correctly.
- Upgrade purchases work.
- Prices and income update correctly.
- Multiple artists work simultaneously.
- Save and load functionality works.
- The interface works on mobile screens.
- No major buttons are non-functional.
- There are no game-breaking errors.

Do not leave placeholder buttons, unfinished systems, or fake interactions.

If something does not work, fix it before finishing.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

Build the complete playable game now.

Do not stop after creating the main menu or visual layout.

Do not replace actual gameplay with descriptions or mockups.

Prioritize a small, polished, fully functional game over an ambitious but unfinished project.

Make sure the final result is fun to play, visually appealing, and technically stable.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Russian-first 2D pixel-art merge and idle tycoon game, “Graffiti Merge: Street Empire,” with functional merging, visible artists painting, upgrades, progression, and local saves.

## Requirements
- Lightweight, offline-capable, responsive for mobile, no accounts or server dependency.
- Russian is the default language; provide a language toggle.
- Functional merge board, item generation, artist jobs/rewards, upgrades, progression, and local save/load.
- Test actual gameplay, mobile layout, and major interactions; fix game-breaking issues.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with a canvas-drawn workshop scene.
- Added a Russian/English toggle, localStorage save, and simplified progression across artists, tools, board, wall, and supply rate.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface, responsive styling, six equipment levels, merge interaction, timed spawning, artist job/drawing loop, rewards, upgrades, progression, collection display, and local saves.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser opened at `http://localhost:8765`; page rendered. Initial console error was only missing `favicon.ico`.

### Active
- Browser/gameplay verification remains incomplete. Browser snapshot showed the expected UI but initial save state had no board items and 35 coins.
- Need verify drag/tap merges, different-level rejection, item spawning, artist completion/rewards, purchases, multiple artists, save/load, English toggle, and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- Initial attempt to seed test state via `playwright-cli eval` failed with a syntax error; `playwright-cli run-code` was then used successfully to seed storage and reload, but the subsequent snapshot still showed the initial state, so test-state setup needs investigation.

## Next Move
1. Inspect browser console and localStorage state, then seed a valid test save and reload.
2. Exercise merge, artists/rewards, upgrade purchases, language toggle, persistence, and mobile layout in Playwright; fix any issues.
3. Save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280, then report test results and note any limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI structure and canvas/board containers.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art workshop styling and responsive layouts.
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, economy, progression, and localStorage persistence.

## Important Context
- Working tree changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 8765`; use `http://localhost:8765`.
- `playwright-cli` Chromium was installed and the browser opened successfully.

## Objective
- Build “Graffiti Merge: Street Empire,” a complete, playable Russian-first 2D pixel-art merge and idle tycoon game.
- Finish real gameplay verification, address any issues found, and capture a current screenshot.

## Requirements
- Lightweight, offline-capable, responsive on mobile; no accounts or server dependency.
- Functional merge board, item generation, visible artist work and rewards, upgrades, progression, and local saves.
- Russian by default with a language toggle.
- Test gameplay, major interactions, save/load, and mobile layout; fix game-breaking issues.

## Decisions
- Implemented as dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript with a canvas-drawn workshop scene.
- Added six equipment levels, timed spawning, artist job/drawing loop, upgrades, collection, progression, Russian/English toggle, and localStorage persistence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main game interface, responsive styling, canvas scene, merge board, economy, upgrades, progression, collection, and local saves.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Installed Chromium and opened the game at `http://localhost:8765`.
- Verified a same-level merge updates the board, an artist finishes a drawing and awards coins, the language toggle switches to English, and purchases affect artists, board size, wall, efficiency, and supply rate.

### Active
- Complete gameplay verification, especially drag-and-drop, mismatched-level rejection, spawning, concurrent artists, save/load across reload, and mobile layout.
- Inspect console errors, fix issues if needed, and capture/read a current JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280.

### Blocked
- Mismatch-merge testing was inconclusive: the reported toast was stale from a prior merge and the selected items had changed. Retest with a clean seeded save.
- Initial test-state seeding was overwritten by the game’s automatic save; the browser test bypassed `Storage.prototype.setItem` temporarily to seed. The test did not establish reliable reload/persistence behavior.
- Browser console has a 404 for `/favicon.ico`; no other errors were observed.

## Next Move
1. Seed a known test save without allowing the running page to overwrite it, then reload and verify its board and balance.
2. Retest drag, tap-to-select merging, invalid merges, spawning, artist rewards/concurrency, all purchases, and persistence; fix any defects found.
3. Test at a mobile viewport and save/read a current `.jpg` screenshot no wider than 1280px.
4. Report verification results and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI structure and canvas/board containers.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art styling and responsive layouts.
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, economy, progression, and localStorage save.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 8765`; game URL is `http://localhost:8765`.
- Playwright browser is open; browser testing used `playwright-cli`.
- One seeded test observed a merge toast and successful artist reward (+20 coins); upgrades purchased successfully in a high-balance test. Mismatch-merge test result is not trustworthy.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

Improve the Existing Game — Graffiti Merge: Street Empire

Continue working on the existing game. Do NOT create a new project or remove working mechanics. Keep the current gameplay, progression, economy and saved progress.


1. Fullscreen Game Layout


- Make the game fill the entire screen.
- All important gameplay elements must fit on one screen.
- Remove webpage-style layout and vertical scrolling.
- Make it feel like a standalone mobile 2D game, not a website.


2. Upgrade Menu


- Add one permanent "Upgrades" button.
- Clicking it opens a compact separate upgrade window.
- Organize upgrades into categories: Artists, Equipment, Work Speed and Workspace.
- Add a close button to return to gameplay.
- Never place long upgrade lists below the game board.


3. Complete Visual Redesign


Replace the current primitive graphics with proper, consistent 2D Pixel Art:


- Detailed pixel-art characters with proper proportions.
- Animated walking, spray painting and drawing.
- A detailed brick wall with actual colorful graffiti artwork, not just words appearing on the wall.
- Pixel-art equipment, backgrounds and interface.
- Consistent urban street-art atmosphere.
- Remove the basic stick-figure characters and browser-page appearance.


4. Fix the New Materials Timer


The timer currently freezes until the player interacts with items.


- Update automatically every second.
- It must work independently of clicks, dragging or other actions.
- When it reaches zero, a new material must actually appear.
- Restart the timer after spawning.
- Fix the underlying update loop and UI refresh, not just the visual countdown.


Important Requirements


- Preserve all existing working gameplay mechanics and progression.
- Keep the entire interface in Russian by default. Do not mix Russian and English text.
- Maintain mobile-friendly touch controls.
- Keep the project lightweight and stable. Avoid unnecessary new systems.
- Test the complete game after making changes: fullscreen layout, upgrade window, animations, timer and all existing gameplay.


Priority: Fix and improve the existing game without breaking anything that already works.

# Skill: OpenCode

# OpenCode

Use this guide as the starting point for work involving OpenCode itself. It
covers the core concepts needed to configure and customize OpenCode, extend it
with plugins, and build integrations with the OpenCode SDK, clients, and API.

Full documentation is available at <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/>. This overview is
only an index of core concepts. Before answering a question about a topic below,
fetch the URL named in that section and use the full page as the source of
truth. Follow links from that page when the question needs more detail. Fetch
<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> first when you need to discover the relevant
documentation page.

A machine-readable documentation index is available at
<https://opencode.ai/v2/llms.txt>.

## Version policy

Always answer for OpenCode V2 unless the user explicitly asks about V1,
legacy OpenCode, or migrating from V1.

Use only <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> documentation as the source of truth for V2.
Do not use <https://opencode.ai/docs/>, which documents V1, and do not use
general web search to resolve a V2 documentation question when the V2 docs or
linked pages cover it. The schema served from
<https://opencode.ai/config.json> accepts both V2 fields and deprecated V1
fields. Never recommend a field it marks deprecated. If V2 documentation is
missing or contradictory, state the uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of falling back to V1.

V1 documentation and syntax may be consulted only when the user explicitly
asks about V1 or when needed as migration input. Outputs and recommendations
must still use V2 unless the user specifically requests a V1 result.

## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Config changes apply without a restart. OpenCode watches config files and
reloads agents, commands, skills, MCP servers, and plugins after a save. The TUI
does the same for `cli.json`. To force a full reload, use `/reload`. Don't tell
the user to restart OpenCode after editing config.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/www/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. Restart it only if it is stuck or unhealthy, not to apply
configuration changes:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

Use OpenCode's built-in `api` command for local requests. It uses the same
discovery and authentication flow as the TUI and may start the background
service when no compatible healthy service is available. It accepts either an
HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:

```sh
opencode api post /api/example --data '{"key":"value"}'
opencode api get /api/example --header 'X-Example:value'
```

Request bodies default to `Content-Type: application/json`. When OpenCode is
connected to an explicit server instead of its managed background service, use
the same configured server and authentication context rather than constructing
an unauthenticated request separately.

See the [full API reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api) for available
endpoints, parameters, request bodies, and response schemas. The
raw [OpenAPI specification](https://opencode.ai/v2/openapi.json) is also
available for code generation and other tooling.

## [Client](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client)

For questions about connecting an application to OpenCode over the network,
fetch the full [client guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client) before
answering.

`@opencode/client` is the generated TypeScript client for the OpenCode HTTP
API. Its methods and types come from the same contract as the API reference.
The default entrypoint exposes Promise-based resource clients and async
iterables for streaming endpoints. The `@opencode/client/effect` entrypoint
exposes typed Effects, Streams, and decoded OpenCode schema values. Its
`Service` API can discover, start, stop, and authenticate with the local
background service from a Node application.

## [SDK](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk)

For questions about embedding OpenCode directly in an application, fetch the
full [SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk) before answering. The SDK
hosts OpenCode in the application without opening an HTTP listener.

Use the [Effect SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/effect) for
Effect applications. For Cloudflare Durable Objects, use the
[Cloudflare SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/cloudflare).

## [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)

OpenCode runs a client and a background server. Start by determining whether a
problem belongs to the client, the shared server, or one project.

- Check the service with `opencode service status` and verify the API with
  `opencode api get /api/info`.
- Compare with `opencode --standalone`, which runs the TUI with a private
  server, to isolate shared-service issues.
- Inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. Filter `role=cli` for
  client startup and `role=server` for sessions, providers, plugins,
  permissions, and tools.
- Run one reproduction with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` when normal logs are not
  sufficient.
- Do not delete or edit the database, service registration, or service config
  while diagnosing a problem. Back up persistent data before inspecting it
  with external tools.
- Redact API keys, authorization headers, prompts, file contents, and other
  sensitive data before sharing diagnostics.

See the [full troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)
for service lifecycle commands, API inspection, log locations, explicit server
connections, issue-reporting details, and local development paths.

Base directory for this skill: /builtin
Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.
Note: file list is sampled.

## Objective
- Improve the existing Graffiti Merge: Street Empire into a fullscreen, mobile-friendly pixel-art game while preserving gameplay, progression, economy, and saved progress.
- Fix the materials timer so it updates and spawns independently of player input.

## Requirements
- Fill the screen with a standalone-game layout; fit key gameplay on one screen without webpage-style vertical scrolling.
- Add a permanent Upgrades button opening a compact separate menu, grouped into Artists, Equipment, Work Speed, and Workspace, with a close button.
- Redesign the visuals as detailed, consistent urban pixel art, including proportioned animated artists, spray-painting/drawing, graffiti artwork, equipment, backgrounds, and interface.
- Keep Russian as the default without mixed-language UI; preserve mobile touch controls and keep the project lightweight.
- Preserve existing working mechanics, progression, economy, and saved progress; test the complete game after changes.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript game and its canvas scene; do not start a new project or remove existing mechanics.
- Existing saves use the `graffiti-merge-save` localStorage key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing game includes merging, timed spawning, artist jobs/rewards, upgrades, progression, Russian/English toggle, and local saves.
- Previously tested merges, spawning, rewards, upgrades, save/load, and mobile layout; fixed a missing favicon.
- `node --check game.js` passed in the previous verification.

### Active
- Implement fullscreen layout and compact categorized upgrade window.
- Redesign the canvas, characters, graffiti, equipment, and interface into consistent pixel art with animation.
- Diagnose and fix the timer/update loop so countdown refreshes independently and materials spawn at zero.
- Retest existing gameplay and new layout/visual features.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`, including the render/update loop, timer UI, and upgrade controls.
2. Implement the fullscreen game layout and modal-style upgrade menu without changing upgrade costs/effects or saved-game data.
3. Improve the existing canvas scene and UI using lightweight pixel-art rendering and animation.
4. Fix and verify independent timer refresh and actual spawning; test merges, purchases, rewards, save/load, touch interactions, and mobile viewport.
5. Check for console errors and confirm no gameplay loss or unintended scrolling.

## Relevant Files

## Objective
- Improve the existing Graffiti Merge: Street Empire into a fullscreen, mobile-friendly pixel-art game while preserving gameplay, progression, economy, and saved progress.
- Fix the materials timer so it updates and spawns independently of player input.

## Requirements
- Fit important gameplay on one screen with no webpage-style vertical scrolling.
- Add a permanent Upgrades button opening a compact categorized window with a close button.
- Redesign the scene and interface as consistent urban pixel art, including characters, artwork, equipment, backgrounds, and animation.
- Keep Russian as the default, retain mobile touch controls, and keep the project lightweight.
- Preserve existing mechanics and saved progress; test the complete game.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript game and canvas; do not remove mechanics or replace the project.
- Preserve the `graffiti-merge-save` localStorage key and save schema.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a permanent upgrades button and modal window with close, backdrop, and Escape-key handling in `index.html` and `game.js`.
- Grouped upgrades into artists, equipment, work speed, and workspace without changing upgrade costs or effects.
- Replaced the page-like styling with a dark, fullscreen responsive game layout in `style.css`, including mobile portrait and landscape layouts.
- Added an independent 250 ms timer check and countdown refresh; spawning now runs outside player input and also catches up when returning to a visible tab.

### Active
- Finish the visual redesign: the canvas still uses the previous wall lettering and simple artist sprites.
- Verify timer behavior, upgrade modal, mobile touch interactions, gameplay, persistence, and absence of scrolling or console errors.
- Check `game.js` syntax and test the rendered game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace the canvas wall lettering and simple figures in `game.js` with more detailed pixel-art mural shapes, proportioned artists, and visible painting/drawing animation.
2. Run `node --check game.js` and launch the game in a browser for desktop and mobile viewport checks.
3. Test timer countdown and spawning, merges, purchases, artist rewards, save/load, modal controls, and scrolling; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure and newly added upgrades modal.
- `style.css`: Newly redesigned fullscreen and responsive game styles.
- `game.js`: Existing mechanics, timer changes, upgrades, save/load, and canvas scene.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing saves use `graffiti-merge-save`; retain the existing data schema.
- The timer runs from a 250 ms interval; if the board is full, spawning is deferred by seven seconds.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn Graffiti Merge: Street Empire into a fullscreen, mobile-friendly pixel-art game while preserving gameplay, progression, economy, and saved progress.
- Ensure materials spawn on an independent timer and verify the complete game.

## Requirements
- Fit gameplay on one screen without webpage-style scrolling.
- Keep a permanent Upgrades button with a compact categorized window and close controls.
- Use consistent urban pixel art, retain Russian as default and mobile touch controls, and keep the project lightweight.
- Preserve mechanics, progression, and the `graffiti-merge-save` localStorage key and schema.

## Decisions
- Retain the dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript game and canvas; do not remove mechanics.
- Keep the existing save key and schema unchanged.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a permanent Upgrades button and categorized modal with close button, backdrop dismissal, and Escape-key handling.
- Restyled the interface for fullscreen responsive layouts, including mobile portrait and landscape.
- Moved supply spawning and countdown updates to an independent 250 ms timer, with visibility-return catch-up.
- Reworked the canvas scene with a brick alley mural, paint cans, detailed pixel-art artists, and animated painting actions.
- Passed `node --check game.js`.
- Browser-checked desktop and 390×844 mobile portrait: no page overflow; upgrades modal opens and Escape closes it with focus returned to the opener.
- Browser-tested merging two level-1 tools: produced a level-2 tool, updated discovery progress, and persisted the result.

### Active
- Complete browser verification of supply spawning/timer, upgrades purchases, artist rewards, save/load, mobile landscape, and console errors or visual defects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://localhost:3002` for supply spawning, purchases, artist rewards, and save/load persistence.
2. Check mobile landscape, inspect console errors and screenshots, and fix any issues.
3. Rerun syntax and browser checks after any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure and upgrades modal.
- `style.css`: Fullscreen and responsive pixel-art interface styles.
- `game.js`: Game mechanics, independent spawn timer, upgrades, persistence, and canvas scene.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The independent supply timer checks every 250 ms; when the board is full, the next attempt is delayed by seven seconds.
- Artists automatically consume board items for jobs, so an empty cell or disappearing item may reflect active gameplay rather than failed spawning.

Fix and Improve the Existing Game — Graffiti Merge: Street Empire

Modify the CURRENT game. Do not create a new project or rebuild working systems from scratch. Preserve all existing progress, gameplay mechanics and working features.


1. Complete Pixel Art Redesign


The game still looks like a linear/vector-style website with primitive characters. Replace this visual style completely with proper 2D Pixel Art.


- Pixel-art characters with detailed sprites and proper proportions.
- Animated walking, working with spray cans and painting graffiti.
- A brick wall featuring actual colorful graffiti drawings, not simple text.
- Pixel-art equipment, objects, backgrounds and interface.
- Consistent retro urban street-art atmosphere.
- Remove stick figures, flat vector graphics and generic website-style elements.


Every visual element must follow the same pixel-art style. Do not simply apply a pixel filter to existing graphics.


2. Fix the Reward and Economy System


Currently, merged items randomly disappear and money appears without a clear explanation. After purchasing upgrades, income almost stops.


Rework and debug this system:


- Clearly define what happens to items after merging.
- Items must not disappear randomly without an understandable reason.
- Clearly show how artists use equipment and produce graffiti.
- Award coins when an artist completes a drawing.
- Show the completed work and the amount of coins earned.
- Make income and upgrade costs understandable and predictable.
- Upgrades must improve performance, not accidentally reduce income.
- Check all reward calculations, item consumption and artist production logic.


The player must always understand where money comes from and what happens to every item.


3. Fix the New Materials Timer


- Update automatically every second, without requiring player interaction.
- When it reaches zero, actually spawn a new item.
- Restart the countdown correctly.
- Fix the underlying update loop and UI refresh.


4. Keep the Existing Interface


- Preserve the current improved screen layout and fullscreen gameplay.
- Keep the compact Upgrades window with its existing categories.
- Do not reintroduce webpage scrolling.
- Keep Russian as the default language throughout the entire game. No mixed Russian and English text.
- Maintain mobile-friendly touch controls.


Important


Do not break working merge mechanics, progression, purchases or saved data. Focus on the visual redesign and fixing the economy and timer. Test everything after changes, especially income before and after purchasing upgrades.


Deliver a fully playable, stable game — not a visual mockup.

## Objective
- Turn Graffiti Merge: Street Empire into a fullscreen, mobile-friendly pixel-art game while preserving gameplay, progression, economy, and saved progress.
- Ensure materials spawn independently and verify the complete game.

## Requirements
- Fit gameplay on one screen without webpage-style scrolling.
- Keep a permanent Upgrades button with a compact categorized window and close controls.
- Use consistent urban pixel art, retain Russian as default and mobile touch controls, and keep the project lightweight.
- Preserve mechanics, progression, and the `graffiti-merge-save` localStorage key and schema.

## Decisions
- Retain the dependency-free HTML/CSS/JavaScript game and canvas; do not remove mechanics.
- Keep the existing save key and schema unchanged.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a permanent Upgrades button and categorized modal with close button, backdrop dismissal, and Escape-key handling.
- Restyled the interface for fullscreen responsive layouts, including mobile portrait and landscape.
- Moved supply spawning and countdown updates to an independent 250 ms timer, with visibility-return catch-up.
- Reworked the canvas scene with a brick alley mural, paint cans, detailed pixel-art artists, and animated painting actions.
- Verified merging, discovery progress, independent supply spawning, hiring and supply-upgrade purchases, artist rewards, and save/load persistence in the browser.
- Checked desktop and mobile layouts, including 390×844 portrait and 844×390 landscape; no page overflow or browser console errors.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. No further work requested; await user direction.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure and upgrades modal.
- `style.css`: Fullscreen and responsive pixel-art interface styles.
- `game.js`: Game mechanics, independent spawn timer, upgrades, persistence, and canvas scene.

metadata.displayText:
Improve Artist Gameplay — Graffiti Merge: Street Empire

Modify the existing game. Do not create a new project or rebuild working systems.


1. Player-Controlled Equipment


Change how artists receive equipment:


- Items must remain on the merge board until the player moves them.
- The player manually drags an item onto an artist or their designated equipment slot.
- Only after accepting the item can the artist take it and begin working.
- Never let artists automatically take random items from the board.
- Never make items disappear without a clear reason.
- If an artist cannot accept an item, return it to its original position.
- Preserve the existing merge mechanics.


2. Visible Artist Activity


Artists must actually do something:


- Walk from their position to the wall.
- Take the supplied equipment.
- Perform a visible painting animation.
- Return to their position when finished.
- Clearly show when an artist is idle, working or waiting for equipment.


3. Real Graffiti Progress


The graffiti on the wall must visibly change during gameplay.


- Each completed job adds a new visible part of the graffiti.
- Show paint gradually appearing on the wall during the painting animation.
- Use actual colorful pixel-art graffiti drawings, not changing words or text placeholders.
- Different jobs should produce visible variations in the artwork.
- The wall should gradually become more decorated as artists complete jobs.


4. Clear Rewards


- Award coins only when an artist completes a painting job.
- Display a clear notification showing the artist and coins earned.
- Show the completed graffiti and reward.
- Do not award random coins for items disappearing or merging.


5. Important Requirements


- Keep the existing merge board, upgrades, progression and economy where possible.
- Preserve saved progress and existing save-data structure.
- Keep the Russian interface.
- Make drag-and-drop work on both desktop and mobile touchscreens.
- Keep the system simple and stable.


Test the complete cycle: merge items → drag equipment to an artist → artist accepts it → walks to the wall → paints visible graffiti → receives coins.


Do not claim completion unless this entire sequence works in the actual game.

## Objective
- Redesign the game’s visuals as consistent retro pixel art with sprites and animations, without changing gameplay or saved data.
- Verify the visual changes in the browser.

## Requirements
- Replace vector/line graphics with pixel-art sprites, including artists with walking, can-holding, and painting animations.
- Redesign graffiti, equipment, objects, backgrounds, and effects in a consistent pixel-art style.
- Keep gameplay mechanics, economy, upgrades, and saves unchanged; verify visually before reporting completion.

## Decisions
- Generate original PNG assets with `assets/generate_pixel_art.py` and integrate them into the existing canvas and interface.
- Use the sprite atlas for character artwork and generated tool PNGs for inventory and interface icons.

## Work State
### Completed
- Generated and integrated the pixel-art background, artist sprite atlas, and six tool icons.
- Updated canvas rendering, painting effects, and interface styling for the pixel-art redesign.
- Verified desktop, mobile, and painting-state views in the browser; `node --check game.js` passed.
- Reset browser local storage to a fresh default save after testing.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Canvas rendering, sprite animation, and game logic.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art styling for the scene and interface.
- `index.html`: Game interface markup and image icons.
- `assets/generate_pixel_art.py`: Procedural asset generator.
- `assets/pixel/`: Generated background, sprite atlas, and tool icons.
- `/tmp/opencode/graffiti-final.png`: Final desktop browser capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/graffiti-mobile.png`: Mobile browser capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/graffiti-painting.png`: Painting-state browser capture.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser tests used a temporary save; afterward, storage was reset to a fresh default save. The pre-test browser save was not recorded and could not be restored.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing Graffiti Merge game so players supply equipment manually and artists complete visible graffiti jobs with clear coin rewards.
- Preserve the existing game systems and save progress while keeping the pixel-art style and Russian interface.

## Requirements
- Keep items on the merge board until the player drags one onto an artist or designated slot; rejected equipment returns to its original position.
- Preserve merge mechanics, upgrades, progression, economy where possible, and existing save-data structure.
- Artists visibly accept equipment, walk to the wall, paint, and return; show idle, working, or waiting states.
- Each completed job adds colorful pixel-art graffiti that appears gradually; no changing-word placeholders.
- Award coins only when painting completes; show the artist and reward. No rewards for merges or disappearing items.
- Support desktop and mobile touch drag-and-drop.
- Test the full merge → supply → accept → walk → paint → reward sequence in the actual game; do not claim completion until it works.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing game and pixel-art assets rather than rebuilding.
- Add an artist-slot area to the existing artist strip; remove the pre-painted mural from the background so job artwork can accumulate at runtime.
- Keep save compatibility while adding or migrating any job state needed.

## Work State
### Completed
- Prior checkpoint’s pixel-art visual redesign and browser verification remain completed.
- Added the `artist-slots` container to `index.html`.
- Changed `assets/generate_pixel_art.py` to generate a blank graffiti wall background.

### Active
- Implement manual equipment assignment and stable drag/drop, including touch interaction and rejected-drop rollback.
- Implement artist job states, movement, painting progress, persistent graffiti additions, and completion notifications/rewards.
- Remove coin rewards from merge bonuses and offline accrual to meet the completion-only reward requirement.
- Test the entire gameplay cycle in-browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update `game.js` to implement explicit equipment assignment, artist state transitions, persistent painting progress, and completion-only rewards.
2. Add styling and Russian status/reward messaging for artist slots and job states.
3. Regenerate pixel assets, run syntax checks, then test the full sequence in the actual browser on desktop and mobile.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing board, merge, save, artist-job, reward, and canvas-rendering logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface; now includes the `artist-slots` container.
- `style.css`: Existing pixel-art interface styles; needs slot/status styling.
- `assets/generate_pixel_art.py`: Background and sprite generator; mural background was changed to blank.
- `assets/pixel/`: Generated background, artist sprites, and tool icons.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing `game.js` automatically removes the lowest-level board item to start jobs, awards merge-combo coins, and grants offline coins; all conflict with the new requirements.
- Existing jobs are serialized in `s.jobs`; preserve compatibility with the `graffiti-merge-save` local-storage save.

## Objective
- Improve the existing Graffiti Merge game so players manually supply equipment and artists visibly complete graffiti jobs for coin rewards.
- Preserve the pixel-art style, Russian interface, merge/progression systems, and save compatibility.

## Requirements
- Keep board items until dragged onto an artist or designated slot; rejected equipment must return to its original position.
- Support desktop and mobile drag-and-drop.
- Show artists accepting equipment, walking, painting, and returning; add gradually drawn pixel-art graffiti that persists.
- Award coins only when painting completes; no merge or offline rewards.
- Test the full gameplay cycle in the actual game before claiming completion.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing game and pixel-art assets.
- Keep the artist slots in the artist strip and the wall background blank for runtime murals.
- Preserve the `graffiti-merge-save` local-storage save structure while adding compatible job and mural state.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added artist slots in `index.html` and translated slot statuses in `game.js`.
- Removed offline coin payouts and merge-combo rewards.
- Added manual board-item assignment to free artist slots, job phases, painting rewards, and persistent mural rendering.
- Added job persistence initialization (`lastJobPersist`) and normalized loaded job fields.

### Active
- Finish debugging lifecycle, persistence, mural placement, and drag/drop behavior.
- Add responsive artist-slot styling in `style.css`.
- Regenerate pixel assets and run syntax checks.
- Verify the full gameplay cycle in an actual browser on desktop and mobile.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` for lifecycle and save bugs; ensure rejected drops preserve the item and completed murals remain in stable positions.
2. Add responsive `.artist-slots` and `.artist-slot` CSS.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, regenerate assets as needed, and test desktop/mobile gameplay in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Merge board interactions, assignment, artist job lifecycle, rewards, persistence, and canvas rendering.
- `index.html`: Game UI and artist-slot container.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art interface and pending artist-slot styles.
- `assets/generate_pixel_art.py`: Pixel-art asset generator, including the blank wall background.
- `assets/pixel/`: Generated wall, artist sprites, and equipment icons.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked.
- `game.js` has not yet been syntax-checked after the recent edits.
- The item-drag logic uses `onPointerUp`, but pointer capture and target detection need browser verification.
- Job painting uses `job.wallIndex` for positioning, while mural persistence currently stores only `{seed, color, level}`; verify positions remain consistent after job completion and reload.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing Graffiti Merge game so players supply equipment manually and artists visibly complete graffiti jobs for coin rewards.
- Preserve the pixel-art style, Russian interface, merge/progression systems, and save compatibility.

## Requirements
- Keep board items until dragged onto an artist or designated slot; rejected equipment must return to its original position.
- Support desktop and mobile drag-and-drop.
- Show artists accepting equipment, walking, painting, and returning; add gradually drawn pixel-art graffiti that persists.
- Award coins only when painting completes; no merge or offline rewards.
- Test the full gameplay cycle in the actual game before claiming completion.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing game and pixel-art assets.
- Keep artist slots in the artist strip and the wall background blank for runtime murals.
- Preserve the `graffiti-merge-save` local-storage save structure while adding compatible job and mural state.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added artist slots and Russian/English slot statuses.
- Removed offline coin payouts and merge-combo rewards.
- Added manual item assignment, artist job phases, completion rewards, and persistent mural rendering.
- Added responsive styling for artist slots.
- Normalized loaded job fields and stored mural `wallIndex` so completed murals keep stable positions.
- `node --check game.js` passed; game loaded in a browser at `http://localhost:3002/`.

### Active
- Debug rejected-drop behavior and desktop/mobile pointer interactions in-browser.
- Verify the full gameplay cycle, including painting completion, coin reward, mural persistence, and reload behavior.

### Blocked
- Browser test setup did not result in the seeded board state; the page still showed an empty board, so gameplay-cycle verification remains incomplete.
- Pixel-art asset validation through Pillow could not run because Python reported `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'`.

## Next Move
1. Seed a playable state using browser storage after the page is loaded, then reload and verify item assignment, job phases, reward, and mural persistence.
2. Test drag/drop and responsive layout in desktop and mobile viewport sizes; fix any issues found.
3. Re-run syntax checks and report only verified behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Merge interactions, artist jobs, rewards, persistence, mural placement, and canvas rendering.
- `index.html`: Game UI and artist-slot container.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art interface and responsive artist-slot styling.
- `assets/generate_pixel_art.py`: Pixel-art asset generator.
- `assets/pixel/`: Generated wall, artist sprites, and equipment icons.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Browser snapshot showed an empty board after attempting to seed `graffiti-merge-save`; no full gameplay cycle has been verified.
- Drag logic uses pointer capture and `onPointerUp`, but target detection still needs browser verification.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing Graffiti Merge game so players manually equip artists, watch them complete graffiti jobs, and earn coins on completion.
- Preserve the pixel-art style, Russian interface, merge/progression systems, and save compatibility.

## Requirements
- Items remain on the board until assigned to an artist or moved; rejected assignments must leave the item in place.
- Support desktop and mobile drag-and-drop.
- Show artists accepting equipment, walking, painting gradually drawn persistent murals, and returning.
- Award coins only when painting completes; no merge or offline rewards.
- Verify the full gameplay cycle in the actual game before claiming completion.

## Decisions
- Keep the existing game and pixel-art assets.
- Keep artist slots in the artist strip and the wall background blank for runtime murals.
- Preserve the `graffiti-merge-save` local-storage structure while adding compatible job and mural state.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added artist slots and Russian/English slot statuses.
- Removed offline coin payouts and merge-combo rewards.
- Implemented manual item assignment, artist job phases, completion rewards, and persistent mural rendering.
- Added responsive styling for artist slots.
- Normalized loaded job fields and stored mural `wallIndex` for stable placement.
- Confirmed the game loads in a browser at `http://localhost:3002/`; one artist slot rendered and no page errors were reported.
- Identified that pointer capture prevents pointer-up events from reaching drop targets; removed the cell-level pointer-up handler and added a document-level `pointerup` listener.

### Active
- Test the updated desktop/mobile drag behavior, including accepted and rejected drops.
- Verify the full job cycle, reward timing, mural persistence, and reload behavior.

### Blocked
- The pointer-up fix has not yet been browser-tested; gameplay completion remains unverified.

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js`, reload the browser, and test dragging a board item onto an artist slot.
2. Verify rejected drops and board-to-board moves preserve or return items correctly; test at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
3. Verify job phases, coin reward only at completion, mural persistence after reload, and report only confirmed behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Drag interactions, artist jobs, rewards, persistence, mural placement, canvas rendering.
- `index.html`: Game UI and artist-slot container.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art interface and responsive artist-slot styling.
- `assets/pixel/`: Wall, artist sprites, and equipment icons.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Browser storage state was overwritten during testing and the board’s item count changed as the spawn timer ran; use a controlled fresh state for verification.
- Browser test exposed pointer capture swallowing target-level `pointerup`; the latest fix uses a document-level listener and still needs verification.

metadata.displayText:
Redesign the entire game using a consistent, high-quality pixel art style.

IMPORTANT: Everything in the game must look pixelated, not just the characters and objects. The entire visual design must follow the same pixel art aesthetic.


1. Visual Style


- Characters must use detailed pixel art sprites.
- All tools, objects, decorations and interactive elements must be pixel art.
- Backgrounds and environments must be fully pixelated.
- All animations must use pixel art sprites and frame-based animation.
- Use consistent pixel resolution and pixel density across the entire game.
- Avoid smooth vector graphics, blurry textures, gradients and modern 3D elements.


2. User Interface


Completely redesign the user interface to match the pixel art style:


- All menus, panels, buttons and windows must look pixelated.
- Use pixel art borders, frames and decorative elements.
- Redesign all icons and indicators in pixel art.
- Make the inventory and item slots look like classic pixel art game interfaces.
- Replace the current green, modern-looking interface with a cohesive pixel art design.
- UI elements must look like they belong in a retro pixel art game, not a modern mobile application.


3. Typography


- Replace all existing fonts with a readable pixel-style font.
- Make all menus, labels, buttons, notifications and counters use pixel typography.
- Ensure that the font supports the Russian language and Cyrillic characters.


4. Colors and Atmosphere


- Use a cohesive retro-inspired color palette.
- Prefer natural, warm and slightly muted colors.
- Avoid excessive neon colors, futuristic blue-purple interfaces and bright gradients.
- Make the game visually charming, playful and atmospheric.


5. Consistency


Every visual element must belong to the same pixel art world. Characters, objects, backgrounds, effects, menus, buttons, fonts and animations must look like parts of one complete game.


Do not change the existing gameplay mechanics, drag-and-drop system, artist behavior or game logic. Only redesign and improve the visual presentation. Preserve all existing functionality.


Apply these changes throughout the entire game, including every screen and menu. Do not leave any old non-pixelated interface elements behind.
